source.title: ScratchDet: Exploring to Train Single-Shot Object Detectors from Scratch
source.authors: Rui Zhu; Shi-Feng Zhang; Xiaobo Wang; Longyin Wen; Hailin Shi; Lie-Feng Bo; Tao Mei

record.file_problem: The supplied text is the full paper, including appendix. It has some apparent OCR or typesetting errors, but the relevant results are readable.
record.tranche_reason: The study applies BatchNorm and reports convergence, training-loss behavior, and detection accuracy for detectors trained from scratch, testing the BatchNorm training-speed claim in object detection.
record.gate_note: The paper reports results for BatchNorm placement and learning rate. Results for other detectors and benchmarks cited from prior work are comparisons, not this study's results. The mAP values measure detection accuracy, not training classification error.
record.test_reason: The study tests V6 in a new setting: object detectors trained from scratch. Its SSD loss trajectories and learning-rate convergence comparisons bear directly on faster optimization and tolerance of higher learning rates.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is broadly accurate. The authors argue that BatchNorm enables stable from-scratch detector training and larger learning rates, freeing architecture design; their Root-ResNet ScratchDet improves detection accuracy on VOC and COCO. Their claim that BatchNorm rather than deep supervision is decisive is stronger than the DSOD endpoint-mAP ablation alone establishes.
record.recipe_differences: The study uses BatchNorm in SSD-style object detectors trained from scratch and compares placements and learning rates. It studies object detection and detection metrics rather than classification error on CIFAR benchmarks.
record.method_sensitivity: BatchNorm placement and learning rate change convergence and detection accuracy. Backbone architecture and downsampling configuration also change detection accuracy, but the paper does not report those as effects on the training classification error named by the versions.

fits_no_version.finding: BatchNorm changes endpoint detection mAP across SSD variants and lowers DSOD mAP when removed.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: BatchNorm can improve final object-detection accuracy when training from scratch.

fits_no_version.finding: VGG16-based Faster R-CNN with BatchNorm trains from scratch to 67.2% mAP; its no-BatchNorm failure comparison comes from prior work.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: BatchNorm permits successful from-scratch training of this Faster R-CNN configuration.

record.peer_reviewed: Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition (CVPR), as stated in the supplied metadata; the paper lists CVPR in references but the supplied text does not state its publication venue directly.
record.problems: The relevant numerical comparisons mainly report detection mAP, not training classification error or a numeric training-speed measure. Training-loss figures are described but their values are not given. The Faster R-CNN comparison does not provide a matched pretrained-versus-scratch setting in the supplied text.
record.rows_left_out: No additional rows for the VOC 2007 ResNet/Root-ResNet architecture sweep or benchmark comparisons: these report detection accuracy effects from backbone and downsampling changes, not BatchNorm's training-speed behavior or the claim versions' named measures. Comparisons to cited prior detectors were not extracted as this study's own results.

untested.parts: Near-zero training classification error on CIFAR-10/100, random or corrupted labels, and model-size, stopping, or regularization conditions.
Teacher-student ReLU optimization, spurious-minimum frequency, and extra student neurons.
Training-error degradation with depth and matched comparisons of plain networks, identity shortcuts, or shortcut-free alternatives.
Comparative initialization effects on propagation, training speed, or trainable depth; Xavier initialization is used without an initialization ablation.
Initial stability thresholds, curvature or sharpness trajectories, catapult recovery, and edge-of-stability behavior.
The named classification settings and Fixup alternative; numerical time-to-accuracy speedups. The reported speed evidence concerns qualitative training-loss convergence.

missing.what: Explicit successful-convergence rows for head BatchNorm at 0.01 and backbone or whole-network BatchNorm at 0.01 and 0.05, paired with the no-BatchNorm failures. Existing mAP rows do not separately record this V6 outcome.
Head-only BatchNorm fails to converge at learning rate 0.05, establishing a placement-dependent limit on higher-rate tolerance.
missing.locator: Table 1, learning rate 0.05, head-only BatchNorm column

record.verdict_notes: Remove the record's limitations based on missing numerical speed measurements and lower accuracy than pretrained Faster R-CNN: neither is evidence against V6. Gradient norms and their fluctuations concern a proposed optimization mechanism, not direct speed measurements. The 84.6 versus 29.7 hour comparison changes initialization and training procedure, so it is not a BatchNorm speed ablation.

versions.untested_parts: CIFAR-10/CIFAR-100 classification error, corrupted or random labels, and model size and early-stopping conditions.
Two-layer ReLU teacher-student problems, spurious local minima, and width differences.

Depth effects in plain versus residual networks and the comparison of shortcuts with no shortcuts. The paper varies backbone structure, but does not test depth-related training error as stated in this version.
Comparisons of initialization schemes for signal propagation, training speed, or trainable depth. The paper states that parameters use Xavier initialization but does not compare initializations.
Training above the stability threshold, curvature or sharpness behavior, and loss recovery or divergence at those learning rates.

The study tests BatchNorm in SSD-like object detectors on PASCAL VOC, including learning-rate and BatchNorm-placement comparisons. It does not test the listed sigmoid MNIST, VGG CIFAR-10, or Inception ImageNet settings, Santurkar et al.'s settings, or Fixup.

rows.subject: VGG16-based Faster R-CNN
rows.operation_detail: Compare convergence without and with BatchNorm.
rows.baseline: Without BatchNorm, training cannot converge; pretrained model obtains 73.2% mAP.
